## Natural history notes

A small fungus-farming ant characterized by its reddish-brown body, rough sculptured surface, spiny thorax, and habit of moving slowly compared with many other ants. In Florida, it is found in sandy habitats such as pine flatwoods, scrub, sandhills, open woodlands, and dry disturbed areas where colonies nest underground in soil. It collects bits of dead plant material, insect frass, and other organic debris to cultivate a specialized fungus inside the nest, which serves as the colony’s main food source.
